description: G2 and G12 (core src/editor/layout/composition/grouping.ts): dressing props by purpose (the archetype table), tied to a building's walls, a cart or a route's edge within the tie reach; blocks (packed clusters over the block area) and grid rows (three or more on a line, evenly spaced) on the square's floor or untied; regrouped into a half-disc off the anchor, or set aside beyond the regroup reach; flora kept off the square. Authored in core (B9's rules are new); every threshold has a case just inside and just past it. Plan frame: IR (x, z) metres.

sources.fixturesFrom: conformance/layout/ground-plan.json (copied byte for byte; the corpus test guards the copy)

cases.name: grouping: Brightwater Vale's dressing round its settled houses
cases.note: Brightwater's 85 props (dressing and rocks) at their settled clearance positions, a disc of half their longest plan side, round the seven settled houses, over the followed plan: the square's goods pile (six barrels and crates packed by the produce stall) is a block and is regrouped at the stall; rocks and walls are not dressing and are left; every dressing prop ends tied to a building, cart or route.

cases.name: audit: Brightwater Vale's dressing as it stood
cases.note: The same props audited as they stood: what was untied, the blocks and rows on the square's floor or untied, flora on the square.

cases.name: purpose: the archetype table, longest prefix by whole segments
cases.note: Which purpose each archetype has: a sub-archetype takes its parent's (crate.small, bench.a), a name that only starts like one does not (prop.containers), and rocks, trees, lanterns, walls and carts are not dressing.

cases.name: tie: a crate whose edge is 2.85 m from a house's wall is tied
cases.note: A 0.8 m crate 2.85 m off a 6 m house's wall, nothing else near: within the 3 m tie, it stays.

cases.name: tie: a crate whose edge is 3.15 m from a house's wall is regrouped at it
cases.note: A 0.8 m crate 3.15 m off a 6 m house's wall, nothing else near: beyond the 3 m tie it is untied, and moves into a cluster off the wall.

cases.name: regroup: an untied crate 19 m from the nearest house is regrouped at it
cases.note: A crate 19 m off the only house: within the 20 m regroup reach it moves to the house.

cases.name: regroup: an untied crate 21 m from the nearest house is set aside
cases.note: A crate 21 m off the only house: beyond the 20 m regroup reach nothing takes it, so it is set aside rather than left loose.

cases.name: pack: four crates 0.3325 m apart by a stall on the square are a block
cases.note: Four 0.8 m crates in a 2 x 2, gaps 0.3325 m, beside a produce stall on the square (2.56 m2): under the 0.35 m pack gap they are one block, so they are regrouped round the stall.

cases.name: pack: four crates 0.3675 m apart by a stall on the square are not packed
cases.note: Four 0.8 m crates in a 2 x 2, gaps 0.3675 m, beside a produce stall on the square (2.56 m2): over the 0.35 m pack gap no two are packed, so each stays tied to the stall.

cases.name: block: a packed cluster covering 1.9 m2 is not a block
cases.note: Four crates of radius 0.344601 m packed 0.1 m apart by a stall on the square, covering 1.9 m2 (each a square of its diameter): under the 2 m2 block area, a small pile, tied.

cases.name: block: a packed cluster covering 2.1 m2 is a block
cases.note: Four crates of radius 0.362284 m packed 0.1 m apart by a stall on the square, covering 2.1 m2 (each a square of its diameter): over it, a block, regrouped.

cases.name: row: three barrels whose middle is 0.19 m off their line are a grid row
cases.note: Three barrels 1.5 m apart on the square, tied to its stall, the middle one 0.19 m off the line of the other two: within the 0.2 m row tolerance they are a grid row and are regrouped round the stall.

cases.name: row: three barrels whose middle is 0.21 m off their line are not a row
cases.note: Three barrels 1.5 m apart on the square, tied to its stall, the middle one 0.21 m off the line of the other two: past it they are not a row and stay.

cases.name: row: four evenly spaced benches in the open, a row; unevenly spaced, none
cases.note: Four benches loose on the square at 3 m spacing are one row of four (not two of three); four more at 2, 3 and 5 m steps along another line are no row.

cases.name: flora: a flower whose edge is 0.57 m outside the square is moved off it
cases.note: A 0.2 m flower 0.57 m outside the square's edge: within the 0.6 m margin, it is moved to the margin off the edge.

cases.name: flora: a flower whose edge is 0.63 m outside the square is left
cases.note: A 0.2 m flower 0.63 m outside the square's edge: past the margin it stays where it grows.

cases.name: flora: ferns and flowers on the square's floor move just off its nearest edge
cases.note: A fern 2 m in from the east edge and a flower 1 m in from the south edge move out across the edge nearest them, to the margin plus their radius outside; a tuft 5 m outside is left; a planter on the square is planting, not flora, and with no house or route to tie to it is set aside.

cases.name: flora: an engine's generated fern points on and by the square
cases.note: trimFloraOffSquare over points: inside the square, 0.57 m outside its edge (within the 0.6 m margin: dropped), 0.63 m outside (kept), far off (kept).

cases.name: anchors: a bench ties to the route, goods to the cart before the house, a sign to the house
cases.note: A bench 1 m off a road's edge ties to the road; a barrel equally near a cart and a house takes the cart (goods prefer a cart); a sign by the house ties to the house; an anvil whose purpose allows no route is regrouped at the house though a road is nearer.

cases.name: cluster: five untied goods and a bench regroup off one house, like by like
cases.note: Five crates and barrels in a grid 8 m off a house and a bench among them: none within the tie, all within the regroup reach of the house; they move into one half-disc off the wall nearest the first, goods together before the seat; the result has no block and no row.

cases.name: cluster: a crate inside a house is pushed out the near wall
cases.note: A house standing on the square, and a packed pile of three 1 m crates on its floor, the first (by id) with its centre inside the house: the pile is a block (3 m2), and the cluster turns outward from the wall nearest that crate, not into the house.

cases.name: cluster: a regrouped crate's spot keeps off a road beside its house
cases.note: The 3.15 m tie case with a road 1 m off the house's wall: the crate's first spot (7.09, 1.81) is on the road, and a spot must clear every anchor (no footprint over a house, a cart or the paving), so the crate stands past the road, still tied to its house.

cases.name: anchors: a bench equally near a route and a house ties to the route, its purpose's first
cases.note: A 1 m bench whose edge is 2.1 m from path z.path's edge and 2.1 m from house a.house's wall. A seat's anchors are a route, then a building, so at equal distance it ties to the route, though the house's id sorts first.

cases.name: anchors: a crate equally near two houses ties to the lower id, whatever the input order
cases.note: A 0.8 m crate midway between houses h2 and h1 (listed h2 first), its edge 2 m from each wall: within the 3 m tie of both, it ties to h1.
